To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vascular AChE activity is of neuronal origin and is localized in basement membranes of capillaries.
the AChE activity in capillaries is of neuronal origin and that the AChES activity in the extracellular space of the brain is due to leakage of AChE from neuronal elements.
AChE-positive endothelial cells and/or pericytes are found in the brain capillaries of several mammals, and that this AChE activity is probably of neuronal origin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution and origin of acetyicholinesterase activity of the capillaries in the CNS of the cat and guinea pig.
the localization of acetylcholine esterase (AChE) in brain capillaries of cat and guinea pig.
the localization of acetylcholine esterase in the brain of cat and guinea-pig, using the histochemical method of Koelle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AChE-positive pericapillary spaces in the brain represent the sites where ACh is degraded by AChE of neuronal origin.
AChE activity is present in endothelial cells and their basement membranes in the capillarization of the brain, that it is of neuronal origin and that it is not involved in the hydrolysis of ACh.
AChE-positive vessels occur in regions with a high density of cholinergic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the capillaries are not only the sites where the brain is supplied with nutrients but also the sites of a neuronal control system which is able to regulate the blood flow to certain regions of the CNS.
AChE is synthesized by neurons in the brain and is transported to and accumulated in capillaries of some brain regions, probably by the axoplasmic transport mechanism.
AChE-positive pericytes and basement membranes are found in capillaries in all brain regions with a neuronal AChE activity, but not in regions with no neuronal AChE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AChE activity can be found in the basement membranes of the capillaries and in the endothelial cells.
the brain capillaries contain AChE activity and that this AChE is probably synthesized by the neurons.
AChE is a marker for capillaries in the CNS.
